title: auth: unify header semantics for project/org keys, scoped tokens, CORS, and request signing (OpenAI compat)
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: The OpenAI-compat layer currently accepts several different auth headers inconsistently which causes surprising errors for customers embedding tokens, using scoped project keys, and when requests go through browser-based clients (CORS). This PR standardizes header semantics across the gateway and openai-compat adapter, adds request signing/nonce support for sensitive operations, and documents migration steps for SDKs. Key goals: 1) Single canonical parsing order for auth headers, 2) Explicit support for scoped tokens (proj- / org- prefixes) and project-level keys, 3) Ensure CORS exposes the right headers and preflight responses, 4) Add optional request signing with x-redwood-signature and x-redwood-nonce and server-side verification hooks, and 5) Maintain backwards compatibility with existing Bearer-style API keys used by OpenAI-compat customers.

release_notes: Standardizes auth header parsing across gateway and OpenAI-compat layer. Adds optional request signing headers (x-redwood-signature, x-redwood-nonce) and explicit CORS expose headers for browser clients. SDKs updated with helper functions. Backwards compatible with existing Bearer API keys but scoped tokens (proj-/org-) are now first-class and recommended for limited-scope credentials.
